top.title: TSU fires Cris Dishman, a former Houston Oilers star, after three years at helm of football program
top.description: Cris Dishman spent three seasons as head coach at Texas Southern, going 14-19. (Jeff Curry/Getty Images) Two days after getting routed in the season finale by Arkansas-Pine Bluff , Texas Southern University announced the dismissal of head coach Cris Dishman on Monday morning. After going 11-11 in his first two seasons at the helm, the former Houston Oilers defensive back went 3-8 with the Tigers this year, including a last-place finish in the SWAC at 2-6. "I want to thank Coach Dishman for his hard work and dedication to Texas Southern University and our football program," TSU athletic director Ashley Robinson said in a statement released by the school. "We wish Coach Dishman well moving forward." Robinson took over at TSU three months ago after leaving the athletic director's post at Jackson State, where he had previously hired Deion Sanders. When Dishman, who replaced Clarence McKinney, was hired in 2024 , he took over a program that had gone though 13 straight losing seasons. He went 5-6 in Year 1, but snapped the Tigers' nine-game losing streak to rival Prairie View A&M in his head coaching debut. The Tigers finally got over the hump in 2025, going 6-5 for their first winning season since 2010. After beating North Carolina Central in this year's season opener, Dishman's third year took a turn with a 52-14 loss to Prairie View A&M in a game that was nationally televised by ESPN. The Tigers won just two of their final nine games, including getting beat 42-17 by Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Saturday. Dishman, 61, played 13 seasons in the NFL, including his first nine with the Oilers (1988-96) where he was a first-team All-Pro selection in 1991. When Dishman was hired in 2024, he was coming off a stint as the defensive coordinator for the XFL's Las Vegas Vipers. He also had previously spent time as an NFL assistant with the Raiders (2005, 2007), Dolphins (2006), Chargers (2009-12) and Cardinals (2017). He also was Baylor's safeties coaching from 2015-16. top.title: Brewers Should Sign Free Agent Pitcher They Traded To Royals Last Offseason
top.description: Free agent pitcher Nick Mears The Kansas City Royals designated Nick Mears for assignment on Nov. 17, and he is now a free agent. The Milwaukee Brewers traded Mears to the Royals last offseason, and a reunion could make sense. The Brewers already lost Dustin May, who was a part of their bullpen in October. They could lose JoJo Romero as well. Bringing back Mears could be a cheap but solid move. Mears had a 3.49 ERA with the Brewers in 2025 and appeared in 63 games for the team. He played a huge role in the Brewers winning the most games in baseball in 2025 and reaching the National League Championship Series. Mears was originally acquired by the Brewers in 2024, but did not really find his footing until the postseason. It was similar to what happened with Romero this year. The Brewers worked with him, and his chase rate was in the 93rd percentile in 2025. In five postseason games with the Brewers between 2024 and 2025, he worked four innings and did not allow any runs. Last season, Mears only pitched in 21 big league games. He dealt with a shoulder injury and a lat injury before ultimately undergoing surgery for thoracic outlet syndrome. He had a 5.12 ERA last season, and he could be open to returning to a team he had success on. The Brewers have a reputation for fixing broken pitchers, and taking a flyer on Mears would be a low-risk move. If he can return to the form he was in during the 2025 season, he would be a great addition to the bullpen.

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jack St. Ivany has made an impact in his first month with the Washington Capitals , chipping in a goal and seven points in 11 games. The defenseman — who was claimed from the Winnipeg Jets on Oct. 24 — was rewarded for his strong play Monday, signing a two-year, $2.35 million contract extension , general manager Chris Patrick announced. The deal carries an average annual value of $1.175 million. Since making his Capitals debut at the end of October, the 27-year-old is tied for second among the team’s defensemen in assists (six) and ranks third in points (seven) and fifth in hits (10), per the official release. He scored his first career goal in a 4-3 victory over the Florida Panthers on Nov. 7. The Manhattan Beach, California native was originally selected in the fourth round, No. 112 overall, by the Philadelphia Flyers in the 2018 NHL Draft. The 6-foot-4 blueliner played collegiately at Yale University and Boston College, amassing 60 points in 115 games. He also won a silver medal with the United States at the 2019 IIHF World Junior Championship. Left unsigned after college, St. Ivany broke into the NHL with the Pittsburgh Penguins after spending a couple of years with AHL affiliate Wilkes-Barre/Scranton, appearing in 14 games in 2023-24 and 19 contests in 2024-25. He split last season between the minors and the NHL, posting seven assists in 20 regular-season games with the Penguins. He was traded to the Jets in exchange for David Gustafsson in June 2026 and made Winnipeg’s opening-night roster out of training camp. St. Ivany made four appearances on the blue line in a third-pairing role before being placed on waivers and subsequently claimed by the Capitals. The right-shot defenseman seems to have found his stride in the nation’s capital, and the extension gives him an opportunity to establish himself as an NHL regular. He’s currently playing on the third pairing ahead of extra defenseman Timothy Liljegren. top.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 28: Kobe Black #6 of the Texas Longhorns celerbates a interception during the fourth quarter of a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 28, 2025 in Austin, Texas. It’s disappointing,” Sarkisian said. “He was having a really good year for us with the position change.” Late in the first half, Black went down grabbing his left knee after attempting to make a tackle on a short completion by Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson. Black spent a significant amount of time down on the field before he was helped into the locker room by trainers. After switching from cornerback to safety during the offseason, Black earned the starting free safety role over senior Derek Williams in the season opener against Texas State, but dealt with injuries throughout the season, missing the UTSA and Ole Miss games, but ultimately starting five times. Black’s season ends with 21 tackles (nine solo) and one pass broken up, steadying a Texas career that was on the brink of ending in disappointment after the Waco Connally product entered the NCAA transfer portal before withdrawing his name and returning to the Forty Acres after the Longhorns made a “strong push” to keep him in the program. As a member of the 2024 recruiting class, Black was a major late addition for Texas as a consensus five-star prospect ranked as the No. 34 player nationally and the No. 5 cornerback in the 247Sports Composite rankings. Black is the fourth major contributor for the Longhorns who is ruled out of the season after Sarkisian left open the possibility that fifth-year defensive tackle Hero Kanu could return in the playoffs after undergoing bicep surgery.

top.title: United States announced as 2031 Women’s World Cup co-host
top.description: ZURICH — The United States is going to be a soccer World Cup host again in 2031 and England will do so for the first time since 1966. FIFA on Monday confirmed the U.S. will lead a four-nation, regional co-hosting of the 2031 Women’s World Cup — with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica — and a UK project led by England was ratified for the 2035 edition. The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments — the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games — and to reinvest all that money in women’s soccer. “This will be the largest women’s sporting event in history,” the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body’s headquarters in Zurich. “Which means we have to deliver.” Rose Lavelle of the United States plays during an international friendly soccer match against Japan in San Jose, Calif., Saturday, April 11, 2026. AP FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women’s soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments . That will bring parity with the men’s World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. The 2027 Women’s World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil. The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica. Spain’s Alexia Putellas, left, Jennifer Hermoso and Irene Paredes celebrate winning the Women’s World Cup final in Sydney, Australia, Aug. 20, 2023. AP The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London. The pair of four-nation co-hosting bids had a clear run in the past 20 months and were approved Monday by acclamation in an online meeting of FIFA’s 211 member federations. The U.S. previously hosted the Women’s World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003. The national team’s tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles. England never hosted a Women’s World Cup which started with the 1991 tournament in China, won by the U.S. In the men’s World Cup, England hosted for the only time in 1966 and won its only title.

top.title: 'There was a time in my career when I was playing all three format': KL Rahul
top.description: NEW DELHI: KL Rahul has opened up about the challenges he faced while trying to balance Test cricket with the demands of ODIs and T20Is. The Indian batter admitted that switching between formats was not easy earlier in his career, as each required a different approach, mindset and preparation. Rahul recently made history with his 136-run knock against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve. He became the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia). He is also only the second Asian opener after Saeed Anwar to achieve the feat. His century was the first by an Indian batter in New Zealand in 12 years. Speaking in a video shared on bcci.tv, Rahul explained how experience and missed opportunities helped him understand the demands of Test cricket. "There was a time in my career when I was playing all three format... I could not make that switch from trying to get bat on ball in T20 and ODI cricket to switching quickly in a week's time to leaving balls and trying to play as late as I possibly can, which is the basics of Test batting," said Rahul. Rahul on preparation and the demands of Test cricket The 34-year-old said Test cricket requires patience, careful preparation and a different way of thinking compared to limited-overs formats. He compared his batting approach to his passion for making coffee, explaining how even a small mistake can affect the final result. "Patience and the preparation, you get one tiny thing wrong and the (coffee) cup is going to taste bad. I think it's the same in Test cricket... one small mistake, one bad shot as a batter and your whole innings can mean nothing even if you've worked hard for three or four hours," he said. Rahul also revealed that he starts preparing mentally five or six months before challenging overseas tours, studying conditions and planning how to tackle them. Rahul opens up about injuries and missed opportunities Despite his historic century, Rahul said the achievement left him emotional and unable to sleep. "Honestly, I've not slept at all the whole night and it's not because of excitement," he said. The batter also expressed disappointment over injuries that have interrupted his career, believing they may have cost him at least 10-15 Test appearances. top.description: Credit: @ChrisCarlin on X / Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images Rutgers had to wait 38 years to beat Penn State again, and Chris Carlin made sure the radio audience heard every one of those years in his voice when it finally happened. The Scarlet Knights stunned the Nittany Lions 25-24 on Saturday before more than 106,000 people at Beaver Stadium, snapping an 18-game losing streak in the series and earning their first victory in State College since 1988. Greg Schiano’s group arrived in Happy Valley at 2-8, an underdog by nearly four touchdowns, and trailed 24-10 heading into the fourth quarter before ripping off 15 unanswered points over the final 10 minutes. The decisive touchdown came out of a finish so improbable it felt borrowed from a backyard game. On the final play of regulation, AJ Surace found Antwan Raymond near the goal line, and with a pair of Penn State defensive backs wrapped around his waist, Raymond flipped the ball to Ben Black III, who strolled the last three yards into the end zone. And in the chaos of the pileup, Carlin and everyone listening on the Rutgers radio network had no idea Black had scored. They found out only when the referee announced the touchdown over the stadium microphone, which drew a stunned “WHAT?!” from Carlin. As requested, Chris Carlin’s call of the touchdown. I had the same exact reaction as Chris when I heard the ref say it was a touchdown over the stadium mic: “WHAT?!” https://t.co/ZbbomROolL — Brian Fonseca (@briannnnf) November 22, 2026 Rather than send out his kicker to tie the game and take his chances in overtime against a team favored by nearly four touchdowns, Schiano kept his offense on the field and put the season, and 38 years of frustration, on a single snap from the 3-yard line. Carlin has been the radio voice of Rutgers football since 2004, which means he has narrated an entire generation of losses to Penn State. Since Rutgers joined the Big Ten in 2014, the Scarlet Knights have lost all 12 conference meetings with the Nittany Lions. Those games covered nearly every kind of heartbreak, from a 28-0 shutout in State College in 2021 to a 40-36 loss at SHI Stadium last November, where Rutgers led in the fourth quarter before Penn State broke its heart once again. After more than a decade of calling those losses, Carlin finally got a finish worth the wait, and the emotion of every one of those afternoons came pouring out of the booth on the two-point try. As Surace rolled toward the Rutgers sideline and floated the ball to Clay Thevenin, who leaked out of the backfield uncovered, Carlin’s voice climbed to a pitch that Rutgers radio had little reason to reach against Penn State for almost four decades. “RUTGERS GOES FOR TWO, FOR THE WIN AND THE UPSET… THEVENIN TO HIS RIGHT… TWO-POINT CONVERSION. HE LOOKS RIGHT… AJ THROWS RIGHT… THEVENIN, THE CATCH! HE’S IN! SCARLET KNIGHTS! … IT’S A NOT-SO-HAPPY VALLEY!” An all-timer from Chris Carlin. A lot of people rose to the moment for Rutgers today. top.title: Francesco Pio Esposito’s rise to becoming a superstar for club and country
top.description: Francesco Pio Esposito’s rise to becoming a superstar for club and country Pio Esposito is the man of the moment, of that there’s no doubt. Inter have struck gold in more ways than one, and on him now hang the hopes of just the future of his club, but also his nation. The 21-year-old has scored a goal in every two appearances for the Nerazzurri , who continue ruing the absence of stalwart Lautaro Martínez, who is out injured. Reaching 30, and getting more injury-prone with age, the Argentine will need to be replaced, and Marcus Thuram is not getting any younger either. No worries, for Esposito seems to be arriving at just the right time, making a name for himself and showing his ability in the Italian top flight well before Lautaro and Thuram’s stars start to fade. What’s even more crucial is his form for Italy. After yet another bout of missing out on the World Cup finals, Gli Azzurri properly hit rock bottom and are beginning to work towards their way back up. Roberto Mancini has identified the need of fresh legs, a young core to prepare the nation for a new era of dominance, with home Euros not too far away. Esposito, thank to his performances, has firmly established himself as a central figure in this new era of Italian football. A reliable out-and-out striker is something the national team has been crying out for for a very long time. Even seasoned stars of the domestic league has struggled to thrive in the national shirt. Esposito, however, seems keen to buck that trend. The outside interest in him, especially from the Premier League , shows teams from across the European football landscape recognise his talent. This is Esposito’s break-out season. With the world at his feet, and the nation’s hopes on his shoulders, it will interesting to see how he charts his journey, with Italy hoping this son of hers to be the next scion of its legendary line-up of forwards. top.title: Discussion: How many more wins do the Panthers need to win the division?
top.description: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 08: Carolina Panthers helmet during an NFL football game between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers on November 8, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers squeaked out a 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday in a game that featured all sorts of twists and turns. The win gets them back to .500. They now have a commanding two game lead over the rest of the NFC South, where every other team is 3-7. The Panthers have seven games left, one against each of the rest of the NFC South, and four against non-divisional opponents. The four other games are significantly harder. They play at the Vikings, home against the Bengals, at the Steelers, and home against the Seahawks. The only one of those four teams that’s not currently in the playoffs is the Seahawks, and they’re the defending Super Bowl champions and have a 6-4 record. It’s going to be hard for the Panthers to find wins there. Meanwhile, the Saints and Buccaneers have much easier paths as they try to catch up to Carolina. The Saints have a game with the Cardinals and a couple of chances to make up ground against the Buccaneers. Those very Buccaneers only have one game left against a team with a winning record—the Rams in Week 17. So that brings us to our question: How many more games do the Panthers need to win to win the division? MY TAKE: 4. Four wins would feel like almost a sure bet to make the playoffs. Someone would have to win out to overtake Carolina straight up and would have to go 6-1 the rest of the way just to tie. Three games might be enough, particularly if one of them is against Tampa Bay on Monday night. If the Panthers lose that, there’s going to be a lot of pressure to create some distance over Tampa given their easier schedule and the tiebreaker advantage they’d have. The easiest way for that to happen is for the Panthers to sweep the three games against their relatively weak divisional foes. Then they’d have to steal just one game from outside of the division, and the best chance for that to happen would be Week 16 against the Steelers.

nigeria.title: Alleged assassination: We want IG to investigate, not Delta police — Omo-Agege
nigeria.description: Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice. Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, made the appeal on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, following an attack on his campaign entourage in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area. He alleged that police officers present during the incident failed to intervene as gunmen opened fire on his team, adding that the attack had heightened fears among opposition politicians in the state. “What we have learned is this: we are not safe here in Delta State. In fact, all members of the opposition party, NDC, most especially, we are all endangered,” he said. Omo-Agege claimed that six truckloads of policemen were deployed to the campaign venue but did not act when the shooting occurred. He accused the state police command of being unlikely to conduct an impartial investigation and urged the IGP to handle the case directly. “We do not expect any justice to come from the police here in Delta State. Neither do we expect any justice to come from the police on this very one,” he said. “We are appealing to the IG to take this matter over directly. We tried to reach him this evening. We couldn’t reach him.” The former lawmaker said he wanted the federal police leadership to investigate the incident, insisting that the state command should not be involved in the probe. He also called for justice for those affected by the attack, saying lives had been lost and several others were receiving treatment in hospitals. “We need justice. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” Omo-Agege said. Despite the incident, he vowed not to abandon his campaign, dismissing suggestions that the attack could intimidate him into withdrawing from the race. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very big mistake and a big lie. Ain’t going to happen,” he said. He, however, appealed to his supporters to remain calm and avoid reprisals, warning that tensions remained high following the attack. nigeria.title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects. The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking. According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility. Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State. He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care. The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide. However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River. Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep. Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million. He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18. According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them. The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime. He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children. nigeria.title: Navy intercepts 89,000 litres of stolen crude, illegal diesel in Rivers
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has intercepted about 35,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and uncovered an illegal refining site containing an additional 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 22 by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder around Okarki Creek and Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area, followed credible intelligence. In a statement on Monday, the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the naval personnel intercepted a wooden boat conveying about 150 sacks containing suspected stolen crude oil. He said a subsequent operation in the adjoining area led to the discovery of an illegal refining site containing approximately 10 dugout pits, 180 sacks and a storage container holding an estimated 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. According to him, the combined volume of petroleum products recovered or identified during the operation was approximately 89,000 litres. “The boat, its contents and the refining site, including the stored products, were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures,” the statement said. The Navy described the operation as part of its sustained campaign to disrupt the supply networks supporting crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the Niger Delta. It said intercepting the suspected stolen crude oil and dismantling associated refining infrastructure would help deny oil thieves access to petroleum resources while addressing environmental degradation and revenue losses. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to intelligence-driven operations to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. It added that operations would continue across the Niger Delta creeks to combat crude oil theft and illegal refining. nigeria.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
nigeria.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. nigeria.title: Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu court Igbo community ahead of 2027 polls
nigeria.description: …Urge national cohesion, economic inclusion By Olasunkanmi Akoni President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development. The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens. He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. “We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future. “Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said. Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State. He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state. “The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos. “We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said. Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution. nigeria.title: APC’ll win three South-East states; Obi will take Abia, Anambra — Bwala
nigeria.description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress will win three states in the South-East in the 2027 general elections, while conceding that Peter Obi could retain a stronghold in Abia and Anambra. Bwala made the projection during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Monday, where he was asked how the ruling party intended to secure victories in the region. He said Obi’s popularity in the two states could make them difficult for the APC to win, but expressed confidence that the party would prevail in the remaining South-East states. “We will struggle in Abia. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said. The presidential aide, however, stressed that his assessment was a projection rather than a definitive prediction, noting that different political actors could arrive at varying conclusions from available data. He said the party was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face difficulties rather than make sweeping claims about its chances. “Where we think we may not, and I use the word advisedly because none of what I’m saying is cast in stone, right? It is projection, and two people from the same political party can have different projections based on our own interpretation of data,” he said. business.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. business.title: Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA Cross River Bank has launched its first bitcoin-backed loans, working with consumer lender LendingUSA to let eligible borrowers take out between $10,000 and $250,000 against their BTC without selling it. The program is the first time Cross River has originated bitcoin-secured loans itself, according to The Block. LendingUSA runs the application platform, and every loan is made by Cross River, a New Jersey state-chartered bank, according to LendingUSA . How the loans work Borrowers can choose a loan-to-value ratio of 30%, 50% or 70%, which sets how much cash they receive against the value of the bitcoin they pledge. LendingUSA defines the ratio as the loan balance divided by the value of the collateral, so a 50% loan against $100,000 of bitcoin would be $50,000. Two repayment options are offered: interest-only or no monthly payments. On an interest-only loan, borrowers make smaller monthly payments that roughly cover interest, with the principal and any remaining interest due at the end of the term. On a no-monthly-payment loan, the full balance plus interest is due at the end. LendingUSA says borrowers can repay early without penalties or fees . Applicants go through a soft credit check, and LendingUSA says approval rests on the crypto being pledged rather than a credit score. The company says funding typically arrives within one to three business days after the collateral is verified. Custody and margin risk A qualified third-party custodian holds the bitcoin for the life of the loan. Once the loan is repaid in full, the collateral is released back to the borrower, according to the company. The terms carry the usual risk of borrowing against a volatile asset. LendingUSA says that if the value of the bitcoin falls, the loan-to-value ratio rises, and borrowers may be asked to add collateral or pay down the debt to avoid liquidation. The company says it will try to notify borrowers first but cannot guarantee it during fast price moves. The timing matters. Bitcoin was trading near $61,000 on Monday morning, so a borrower at the 70% tier would have far less room before a collateral call than one at the 30% tier. Lower ratios leave a bigger cushion but unlock less cash per bitcoin pledged. LendingUSA markets the loans for uses such as debt consolidation, home improvements and large purchases. The company says it has served more than 200,000 borrowers across its lending business, and the crypto product is its first expansion into digital asset-backed loans. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. sports.title: TSU fires Cris Dishman, a former Houston Oilers star, after three years at helm of football program
sports.description: Cris Dishman spent three seasons as head coach at Texas Southern, going 14-19. (Jeff Curry/Getty Images) Two days after getting routed in the season finale by Arkansas-Pine Bluff , Texas Southern University announced the dismissal of head coach Cris Dishman on Monday morning. After going 11-11 in his first two seasons at the helm, the former Houston Oilers defensive back went 3-8 with the Tigers this year, including a last-place finish in the SWAC at 2-6. "I want to thank Coach Dishman for his hard work and dedication to Texas Southern University and our football program," TSU athletic director Ashley Robinson said in a statement released by the school. "We wish Coach Dishman well moving forward." Robinson took over at TSU three months ago after leaving the athletic director's post at Jackson State, where he had previously hired Deion Sanders. When Dishman, who replaced Clarence McKinney, was hired in 2024 , he took over a program that had gone though 13 straight losing seasons. He went 5-6 in Year 1, but snapped the Tigers' nine-game losing streak to rival Prairie View A&M in his head coaching debut. The Tigers finally got over the hump in 2025, going 6-5 for their first winning season since 2010. After beating North Carolina Central in this year's season opener, Dishman's third year took a turn with a 52-14 loss to Prairie View A&M in a game that was nationally televised by ESPN. The Tigers won just two of their final nine games, including getting beat 42-17 by Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Saturday. Dishman, 61, played 13 seasons in the NFL, including his first nine with the Oilers (1988-96) where he was a first-team All-Pro selection in 1991. When Dishman was hired in 2024, he was coming off a stint as the defensive coordinator for the XFL's Las Vegas Vipers. He also had previously spent time as an NFL assistant with the Raiders (2005, 2007), Dolphins (2006), Chargers (2009-12) and Cardinals (2017). He also was Baylor's safeties coaching from 2015-16. sports.title: Brewers Should Sign Free Agent Pitcher They Traded To Royals Last Offseason
sports.description: Free agent pitcher Nick Mears The Kansas City Royals designated Nick Mears for assignment on Nov. 17, and he is now a free agent. The Milwaukee Brewers traded Mears to the Royals last offseason, and a reunion could make sense. The Brewers already lost Dustin May, who was a part of their bullpen in October. They could lose JoJo Romero as well. Bringing back Mears could be a cheap but solid move. Mears had a 3.49 ERA with the Brewers in 2025 and appeared in 63 games for the team. He played a huge role in the Brewers winning the most games in baseball in 2025 and reaching the National League Championship Series. Mears was originally acquired by the Brewers in 2024, but did not really find his footing until the postseason. It was similar to what happened with Romero this year. The Brewers worked with him, and his chase rate was in the 93rd percentile in 2025. In five postseason games with the Brewers between 2024 and 2025, he worked four innings and did not allow any runs. Last season, Mears only pitched in 21 big league games. He dealt with a shoulder injury and a lat injury before ultimately undergoing surgery for thoracic outlet syndrome. He had a 5.12 ERA last season, and he could be open to returning to a team he had success on. The Brewers have a reputation for fixing broken pitchers, and taking a flyer on Mears would be a low-risk move. If he can return to the form he was in during the 2025 season, he would be a great addition to the bullpen.

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jack St. Ivany has made an impact in his first month with the Washington Capitals , chipping in a goal and seven points in 11 games. The defenseman — who was claimed from the Winnipeg Jets on Oct. 24 — was rewarded for his strong play Monday, signing a two-year, $2.35 million contract extension , general manager Chris Patrick announced. The deal carries an average annual value of $1.175 million. Since making his Capitals debut at the end of October, the 27-year-old is tied for second among the team’s defensemen in assists (six) and ranks third in points (seven) and fifth in hits (10), per the official release. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Averaging a shade over 14 minutes per game between Washington and Winnipeg, St. Ivany was the first player in franchise history to record multiple assists in each of his first two games with the Caps. He scored his first career goal in a 4-3 victory over the Florida Panthers on Nov. 7. The Manhattan Beach, California native was originally selected in the fourth round, No. 112 overall, by the Philadelphia Flyers in the 2018 NHL Draft. The 6-foot-4 blueliner played collegiately at Yale University and Boston College, amassing 60 points in 115 games. He also won a silver medal with the United States at the 2019 IIHF World Junior Championship. Left unsigned after college, St. Ivany broke into the NHL with the Pittsburgh Penguins after spending a couple of years with AHL affiliate Wilkes-Barre/Scranton, appearing in 14 games in 2023-24 and 19 contests in 2024-25. He split last season between the minors and the NHL, posting seven assists in 20 regular-season games with the Penguins. He was traded to the Jets in exchange for David Gustafsson in June 2026 and made Winnipeg’s opening-night roster out of training camp. St. Ivany made four appearances on the blue line in a third-pairing role before being placed on waivers and subsequently claimed by the Capitals. The right-shot defenseman seems to have found his stride in the nation’s capital, and the extension gives him an opportunity to establish himself as an NHL regular. He’s currently playing on the third pairing ahead of extra defenseman Timothy Liljegren. It remains to be seen what role he will play when Rasmus Sandin is ready to return from a torn ACL the Swede sustained in April. Losers of five straight, the Capitals are back in action against the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday night. sports.title: Texas S Kobe Black out for season
sports.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 28: Kobe Black #6 of the Texas Longhorns celerbates a interception during the fourth quarter of a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 28, 2025 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — During his Monday press conference, Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian confirmed a report from On Texas Football that junior safety Kobe Black will miss the remainder of the season after suffering an injury during Saturday’s win over the Arkansas Razorbacks. “I hate it for him. It’s disappointing,” Sarkisian said. “He was having a really good year for us with the position change.” Late in the first half, Black went down grabbing his left knee after attempting to make a tackle on a short completion by Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson. Black spent a significant amount of time down on the field before he was helped into the locker room by trainers. After switching from cornerback to safety during the offseason, Black earned the starting free safety role over senior Derek Williams in the season opener against Texas State, but dealt with injuries throughout the season, missing the UTSA and Ole Miss games, but ultimately starting five times. Black’s season ends with 21 tackles (nine solo) and one pass broken up, steadying a Texas career that was on the brink of ending in disappointment after the Waco Connally product entered the NCAA transfer portal before withdrawing his name and returning to the Forty Acres after the Longhorns made a “strong push” to keep him in the program. As a member of the 2024 recruiting class, Black was a major late addition for Texas as a consensus five-star prospect ranked as the No. 34 player nationally and the No. 5 cornerback in the 247Sports Composite rankings. Black is the fourth major contributor for the Longhorns who is ruled out of the season after Sarkisian left open the possibility that fifth-year defensive tackle Hero Kanu could return in the playoffs after undergoing bicep surgery.

sports.title: United States announced as 2031 Women’s World Cup co-host
sports.description: ZURICH — The United States is going to be a soccer World Cup host again in 2031 and England will do so for the first time since 1966. FIFA on Monday confirmed the U.S. will lead a four-nation, regional co-hosting of the 2031 Women’s World Cup — with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica — and a UK project led by England was ratified for the 2035 edition. The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments — the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games — and to reinvest all that money in women’s soccer. “This will be the largest women’s sporting event in history,” the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body’s headquarters in Zurich. “Which means we have to deliver.” Rose Lavelle of the United States plays during an international friendly soccer match against Japan in San Jose, Calif., Saturday, April 11, 2026. AP FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women’s soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments . That will bring parity with the men’s World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. The 2027 Women’s World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil. The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica. Spain’s Alexia Putellas, left, Jennifer Hermoso and Irene Paredes celebrate winning the Women’s World Cup final in Sydney, Australia, Aug. 20, 2023. AP The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London. The pair of four-nation co-hosting bids had a clear run in the past 20 months and were approved Monday by acclamation in an online meeting of FIFA’s 211 member federations. The U.S. previously hosted the Women’s World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003. The national team’s tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles. England never hosted a Women’s World Cup which started with the 1991 tournament in China, won by the U.S. In the men’s World Cup, England hosted for the only time in 1966 and won its only title.

sports.title: Nick Bosa’s postgame gesture to Mexico City 49ers fans speaks volumes
sports.description: San Francisco 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa was awash in boos from Mexico City fans when being introduced Sunday. This appeared to be the byproduct of Bosa’s comments from earlier in the week, when he made a request about how fans at the game should cheer . “I think we need some, like, information given to the fans so they know when to cheer. ’Cause, uh, they just chant the whole time,” Bosa said Wednesday. Nick Bosa (No. 97) of the San Francisco 49ers said he wants “information given to the fans so they know when to cheer.” Getty Images “But yeah, if we could kind of teach them — no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques — but if they could cheer when we’re on defense, that would be great,” he added. View this post on Instagram The comments likely irked some fans who plausibly felt Bosa’s comments implied fans in Mexico didn’t know the rules of American football or when the correct time to cheer was. However, some others didn’t seem to mind what Bosa said — and there were certainly many who showered him with love in Mexico City, as seen in a video from Instagram user @49ers.cam, showing Bosa approaching the stands after beating the Vikings and throwing his gloves into the crowd. Bosa engaging with Niners fans in Mexico City after beating the Minnesota Vikings. The star edge rusher throwing his gloves into the crowd after the 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Fans were cheering him on throughout the exchange, as the camera then followed Bosa as he walked into the locker room, high-fiving young fans. The video speaks volumes in that some of the backlash to Bosa’s comments was overblown . Or at least not every 49ers fan was offended by what he said, even those who were in Mexico City. sports.title: 'There was a time in my career when I was playing all three format': KL Rahul
sports.description: NEW DELHI: KL Rahul has opened up about the challenges he faced while trying to balance Test cricket with the demands of ODIs and T20Is. The Indian batter admitted that switching between formats was not easy earlier in his career, as each required a different approach, mindset and preparation. Rahul recently made history with his 136-run knock against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve. He became the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia). He is also only the second Asian opener after Saeed Anwar to achieve the feat. His century was the first by an Indian batter in New Zealand in 12 years. Speaking in a video shared on bcci.tv, Rahul explained how experience and missed opportunities helped him understand the demands of Test cricket. "There was a time in my career when I was playing all three format... I could not make that switch from trying to get bat on ball in T20 and ODI cricket to switching quickly in a week's time to leaving balls and trying to play as late as I possibly can, which is the basics of Test batting," said Rahul. Rahul on preparation and the demands of Test cricket The 34-year-old said Test cricket requires patience, careful preparation and a different way of thinking compared to limited-overs formats. He compared his batting approach to his passion for making coffee, explaining how even a small mistake can affect the final result. "Patience and the preparation, you get one tiny thing wrong and the (coffee) cup is going to taste bad. I think it's the same in Test cricket... one small mistake, one bad shot as a batter and your whole innings can mean nothing even if you've worked hard for three or four hours," he said. Rahul also revealed that he starts preparing mentally five or six months before challenging overseas tours, studying conditions and planning how to tackle them. Rahul opens up about injuries and missed opportunities Despite his historic century, Rahul said the achievement left him emotional and unable to sleep. "Honestly, I've not slept at all the whole night and it's not because of excitement," he said. The batter also expressed disappointment over injuries that have interrupted his career, believing they may have cost him at least 10-15 Test appearances. Having played 71 Tests, Rahul hopes to remain fit, continue scoring runs and finish the final phase of his career strongly.

sports.title: 'Not So Happy Valley!': Chris Carlin erupts as Rutgers stuns Penn State
sports.description: Credit: @ChrisCarlin on X / Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images Rutgers had to wait 38 years to beat Penn State again, and Chris Carlin made sure the radio audience heard every one of those years in his voice when it finally happened. The Scarlet Knights stunned the Nittany Lions 25-24 on Saturday before more than 106,000 people at Beaver Stadium, snapping an 18-game losing streak in the series and earning their first victory in State College since 1988. Greg Schiano’s group arrived in Happy Valley at 2-8, an underdog by nearly four touchdowns, and trailed 24-10 heading into the fourth quarter before ripping off 15 unanswered points over the final 10 minutes. The decisive touchdown came out of a finish so improbable it felt borrowed from a backyard game. On the final play of regulation, AJ Surace found Antwan Raymond near the goal line, and with a pair of Penn State defensive backs wrapped around his waist, Raymond flipped the ball to Ben Black III, who strolled the last three yards into the end zone. And in the chaos of the pileup, Carlin and everyone listening on the Rutgers radio network had no idea Black had scored. They found out only when the referee announced the touchdown over the stadium microphone, which drew a stunned “WHAT?!” from Carlin. As requested, Chris Carlin’s call of the touchdown. I had the same exact reaction as Chris when I heard the ref say it was a touchdown over the stadium mic: “WHAT?!” https://t.co/ZbbomROolL — Brian Fonseca (@briannnnf) November 22, 2026 Rather than send out his kicker to tie the game and take his chances in overtime against a team favored by nearly four touchdowns, Schiano kept his offense on the field and put the season, and 38 years of frustration, on a single snap from the 3-yard line. Carlin has been the radio voice of Rutgers football since 2004, which means he has narrated an entire generation of losses to Penn State. Since Rutgers joined the Big Ten in 2014, the Scarlet Knights have lost all 12 conference meetings with the Nittany Lions. Those games covered nearly every kind of heartbreak, from a 28-0 shutout in State College in 2021 to a 40-36 loss at SHI Stadium last November, where Rutgers led in the fourth quarter before Penn State broke its heart once again. After more than a decade of calling those losses, Carlin finally got a finish worth the wait, and the emotion of every one of those afternoons came pouring out of the booth on the two-point try. As Surace rolled toward the Rutgers sideline and floated the ball to Clay Thevenin, who leaked out of the backfield uncovered, Carlin’s voice climbed to a pitch that Rutgers radio had little reason to reach against Penn State for almost four decades. “RUTGERS GOES FOR TWO, FOR THE WIN AND THE UPSET… THEVENIN TO HIS RIGHT… TWO-POINT CONVERSION. The same could be said about star receiver A.J. Brown who returned to the lineup in Week 10 after missing nearly a month of action due to injury. His absence, and the lack of production in his return (two catches for 27 yards on six targets) has further fueled rumors that the Tennessee Titans were eager to move on from the three-time Pro Bowl receiver because they felt his knees only had two more years left before breaking down at the time. Well, he’s since helped win a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles, but he’s now five years removed from the trade and has since earned two more Pro Bowl nods. Still, the fact that Brown has missed six games due to injury doesn’t help his case. sports.title: Discussion: How many more wins do the Panthers need to win the division?
sports.description: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 08: Carolina Panthers helmet during an NFL football game between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers on November 8, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers squeaked out a 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday in a game that featured all sorts of twists and turns. The win gets them back to .500. They now have a commanding two game lead over the rest of the NFC South, where every other team is 3-7. The Panthers have seven games left, one against each of the rest of the NFC South, and four against non-divisional opponents. The four other games are significantly harder. They play at the Vikings, home against the Bengals, at the Steelers, and home against the Seahawks. The only one of those four teams that’s not currently in the playoffs is the Seahawks, and they’re the defending Super Bowl champions and have a 6-4 record. It’s going to be hard for the Panthers to find wins there. Meanwhile, the Saints and Buccaneers have much easier paths as they try to catch up to Carolina. The Saints have a game with the Cardinals and a couple of chances to make up ground against the Buccaneers. Those very Buccaneers only have one game left against a team with a winning record—the Rams in Week 17. So that brings us to our question: How many more games do the Panthers need to win to win the division? MY TAKE: 4. Four wins would feel like almost a sure bet to make the playoffs. Someone would have to win out to overtake Carolina straight up and would have to go 6-1 the rest of the way just to tie. Three games might be enough, particularly if one of them is against Tampa Bay on Monday night. If the Panthers lose that, there’s going to be a lot of pressure to create some distance over Tampa given their easier schedule and the tiebreaker advantage they’d have. The easiest way for that to happen is for the Panthers to sweep the three games against their relatively weak divisional foes. Then they’d have to steal just one game from outside of the division, and the best chance for that to happen would be Week 16 against the Steelers.

sports.description: FORT MYERS, FLORIDA - MARCH 7: Johan Oviedo #29 of the Boston Red Sox looks on in the dugout before a spring training game against the Tampa Bay Rays at JetBlue Park at Fenway South on March 7, 2026 in Fort Myers, Florida. (Photo by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Nov. 20 the Diamondbacks acquired right-hander Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later or cash. It’s an easy trade to scroll past: a 28-year-old starter who struggles to throw strikes and has thrown 44 big-league innings since 2023, coming off Tommy John surgery, a lat strain and an elbow strain. But a year ago this exact pitcher cost Boston its No. 6 prospect. The reason is likely tied strongly to one pitch, and it’s still there. The Fastball That Changed In 2023, Oviedo’s four-seamer was hard and flat. It averaged 95.8 mph with 10.2 inches of induced vertical break (IVB), well below average for a four-seamer that firm. Despite the velocity and the elite extension from Oviedo’s massive body at 6’6”, hitters didn’t miss it: an 18% whiff rate per swing, and a Stuff+ of 91, 34th percentile among MLB four-seamers. The breaking balls weren’t the problem. In 2023 his slider (+11.2 runs) and curveball (+4.6) saved about 16 runs combined, while the four-seamer cost him 6.4. Per pitch, the slider and curve were above average (62nd and 70th percentile in run value per 100), and much of the +16 comes from volume: together they were half his pitches. This put Oviedo in the 98th percentile in baseball on statcast’s breaking run value. Despite having a well below average fastball by stuff+ in just the 34th percentile, Oviedo was able to rely on his breaking pitches to pitch to a respectable 4.31 ERA. He would then miss all of 2024 after Tommy John surgery. When he came back in August 2025, the fastball was very different: His IVB jumps off the page. Five extra inches of ride at the same velocity is a big change. What’s interesting is how he got it. The usual way to add ride is to raise the arm slot and get more over the top. Oviedo went the other way: his arm angle dropped from about 28° to 24° and his release point fell about 2.6 inches. The ride came from the spin itself. Less of his movement went sideways (run fell by almost 4 inches) and more went straight up. That’s the sign of truer backspin. The combination is what hitters hate. A lower release plus more carry means the ball arrives on a flatter plane (-4.16° vs -5.05°), so it stays above barrels at the top of the zone. Add elite extension and the 95.5 mph plays like about 97. How Rare is a Gain Like This? technology.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
technology.description: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

technology.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
technology.description: The Ancient Thracian heartland of Bulgaria says it has shut down a cyberespionage operation that gave intruders access to government networks for five years – the longest-running known campaign against its administration. Bulgaria's Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation said the unauthorized and officially unattributed attackers first gained access to infrastructure used by government institutions to exchange information in 2021. It explained that the intrusion went unnoticed for so long because "the previous means of protection did not work as a single, integrated system," and that without a new, recently installed product, it may have gone undetected for much longer. "The incident was discovered thanks to the new national cybersecurity system, which for the first time provides a single picture of what is happening in state networks," the ministry added. "Without it, this activity would most likely have remained hidden for an indefinite period of time." Bulgaria acknowledged that "sensitive information related to the work of the state" was accessed, but did not specify the scale of the compromise. Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev said attackers had downloaded more than 130 GB of data over five years. He also put the volume at 62 million pages. The Register contacted the Bulgarian government for confirmation of these numbers. The ministry said that it has not yet found any evidence that citizens' personal data was compromised, and that the affected infrastructure "will be under increased surveillance for 90 days" in case the attackers try to regain access. Vasilev said multiple international hacking groups had accessed government systems since 2021. He did not specify the names of these groups, however, nor did he name any specific countries that may have been involved. In a follow-up interview with bTV , Vasilev blamed political instability and frequent changes of ministerial leadership for leaving government systems inadequately protected. A representative of the Progressive Bulgaria party, which back in May won Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years, Vasilev said the "constant change of leadership" means "important things for the state do not actually happen." Vasilev said the intrusion was discovered over the summer as the national cybersecurity system was upgraded, and that teams had spent the past three to four months removing the attackers. ®

technology.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
technology.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
science.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067).
